## Further Reading

Anscombe, F. J. (1973). Graphs in statistical analysis. *The American Statistician*, *27*(1), 17–21. <https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.1973.10478966> A short classic that presents four small data sets with the same means, variances, correlation, and regression line, whose plots look completely different. It is the standard argument for looking at data before trusting the statistics that summarize it.

Datar, S. M., & Rajan, M. V. (2021). *Horngren's cost accounting: A managerial emphasis* (17th ed.). Pearson. <https://www.pearson.com/en-us/pearsonplus/p/9780136713845> A widely used cost accounting text. Its chapter on customer-profitability and sales-variance analysis develops the sales-volume, sales-mix, and sales-quantity variances against a budget, the budget-based counterpart of the margin bridge in this chapter.

Domino, M. A., Schrag, D., Webinger, M., & Troy, C. (2021). Linking data analytics to real-world business issues: The power of the pivot table. *Journal of Accounting Education*, *57*, Article 100744. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaccedu.2021.100744> A teaching case in which you use pivot tables to analyze a moderately large and complex data set from a privately owned company and write memorandums to managers about their concerns. It practices the same move from summary to recommendation as this chapter.

Microsoft. (2026a). *Calculate values in a PivotTable*. Microsoft Support. <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/calculate-values-in-a-pivottable-11f41417-da80-435c-a5c6-b0185e59da77> Microsoft's reference for summary functions, calculated fields, and calculated items in PivotTables. It explains why a calculated field works on the sums of its fields while a calculated item works on individual records, with examples.

Microsoft. (2026b). *Show different calculations in PivotTable value fields*. Microsoft Support. <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/show-different-calculations-in-pivottable-value-fields-014d2777-baaf-480b-a32b-98431f48bfec> A description of every Show Values As option, from % of Grand Total to Index, with the base field and base item each one needs.

Palocsay, S. W., Markham, I. S., & Markham, S. E. (2010). Utilizing and teaching data tools in Excel for exploratory analysis. *Journal of Business Research*, *63*(2), 191–206. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbusres.2009.03.008> An article that presents Excel as an introductory tool for business intelligence and exploratory analysis, covering Excel as a database, PivotTables and PivotCharts, and importing data. It was written for an older version of Excel, but its approach to exploring business data carries over.

Public Company Accounting Oversight Board. (n.d.). *AS 2305: Substantive analytical procedures*. <https://pcaobus.org/oversight/standards/auditing-standards/details/AS2305> The auditing standard that governs analytical procedures used as substantive tests in audits of public companies. It explains how auditors develop expectations, decide how large a difference can be accepted without further investigation, and evaluate significant unexpected differences.
